title: The Seat of Our Pants by Ethan Lipton at The Public #theseatofourpant...
transcript: The Seat of Our Pants at The Public is a well crafted fever dream. Adapted by Ethan Lipton and based on the Thornton Wilder play The Skin of Our Teeth, it follows the Antrobus family through a series of catastrophes. It's an allegory for humanity and how our very existence is always on the edge. And yet, despite all odds, we carry on. It's absurd by design, and incorporates a self-awareness through its satirical material and its occasional fourth wall breaks. The production is most successful when it leans into its eccentricities and sarcasms, and less so when it veers too far into earnestness and sentimentalities. But aside from its unevenness in tone and occasionally in its pacing, it's a good time. I was familiar with The Skin of Our Teeth, so I was prepared for the twisty and absurd nature of the plot, but what I didn't necessarily expect was for the incorporation of music to work so well here. Melodically and harmonically, it's one of my favourite new scores I've heard in recent memory, and it's excellently performed. Keep an ear out for some great harmonies toward the top of Act 3 from Ruthie Ann Miles, Micaela Diamond, and Amina Faye. As an adaptation, I think this is pretty successful — it's just as wonderfully strange as its source material. That said, if you're not a fan of the source material, I wouldn't necessarily expect you to be a fan of this. But for anyone who's not familiar with it, I'd encourage you to buckle up and see what you think. With that another Playbill for my collection.
